reasons: The cited paragraph is indeed a bare successors-and-assigns clause with no consent standard, so the deviation call (missing asymmetric allocation) is accurate and the rationale correctly notes no change-of-control termination/re-pricing right exists elsewhere, so no walk-away trigger.

The redline reaches the preferred position in full: Customer (Company) may assign to affiliates and M&A successors without consent; HDI needs Customer consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Customer competitor; Customer change of control is not an assignment and confers no HDI termination or re-pricing right.
Edit is additive and minimal — the original sentence is preserved and only the missing allocations are appended; no conflict with the existing no-third-party-rights language.
Comment is accurate, uses the required prefix and first-person plural tone, explains the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the mutual notice-based fallback.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and the successor/affiliate carve-out is present; party aliases are used correctly (Company = us, HDI = Vendor).
